title: Acceptance and Committment Therapy Combined With Ketamine in Difficult-to-Treat Depression.
official: Recovery-focused Acceptance and Commitment Therapy Combined With Ketamine (K-ACT) for Patients With Difficult-to-treat Depression: a Feasibility Study.
summary: Ketamine is often used to treat depression where standard treatments have failed. Yet, even with ketamine, depression can persist and make it difficult to keep up with life. This study examines whether it is practical, safe and helpful to use a talk therapy (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, ACT) in patients with difficult-to-treat depression receiving ketamine through the Ketamine Intervention Program at UBC Hospital. Researchers expect that combining ACT plus Ketamine ("K-ACT") will be feasible, safe, and will help patients functioning better in their daily lives, feeling that they are recovering, and having fewer symptoms of depression.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

To participate in this study, individuals must be eligible for and enrolled in the Ketamine Intervention Program (KIP) at UBC Hospital, an ongoing clinical program for difficult-to-treat depression, which has the following inclusion criteria:

1. Be of age 18 or older.
2. Have a DSM-5-TR diagnosis of major depressive disorder (MDD) or bipolar disorder (BD), in a current major depressive episode.
3. If diagnosed with MDD, have failed adequate trials of at least 2 antidepressants and 1 adjunctive medication(s); if BD, having failed adequate trials of at least 3 agents for bipolar depression.
4. Have a referral from a community psychiatrist who agrees to follow the patient throughout the entire trial.
5. Have the ability to provide informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

Individuals will not be eligible for the K-ACT study if they are deemed ineligible for enrollment with the KIP at UBC Hospital due to meeting any of the following existing exclusion criteria:

1. They are experiencing active psychosis.
2. They have: any of history of ketamine use disorder; a history of alcohol or other substance use disorder in the past 6 months; dementia or delirium; unstable medical conditions; uncontrolled hypertension; a history of seizures in the past 6 months; a history of elevated intracranial pressure/aneurysmal disease/arteriovenous malformation/intracranial hemorrhage.
3. They are currently pregnant or breastfeeding.
4. They have an allergy to ketamine.

Exclusion criteria specific to the K-ACT study include:

1. Currently undergoing ACT.
2. Past ACT within last 12 months.
3. Currently undergoing non-ACT structured psychotherapy (e.g., cognitive-behavioural therapy).
